st: Pound the steak slices thin between sheets of plastic wrap, then season both sides with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Cook the bacon in a large skillet over medium heat for [[8 minutes]] until crisp, then move it to a plate.
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in the same skillet over high heat and sear the steak slices for 1 to 2 minutes per side until browned. Move them to a plate.
Lower the heat to medium, melt [[1 tbsp]] butter and fry the eggs until the whites are set, about 3 minutes.
Toast the cut sides of the rolls in a dry pan or under the broiler until golden.
Spread [[1 tbsp]] mayonnaise on each roll bottom, then add lettuce and tomato slices.
Layer on the steak, ham, bacon and mozzarella, then add a fried egg on each.
Cover the top of each sandwich with the roll lid and press down. Serve hot with fries if you like.
Take the meat out of the fridge [[30 minutes]] ahead so it is not ice cold when it hits the grill.
Light the charcoal in a grill and let it burn until covered in gray ash, about 30 minutes. Spread the coals to one side.
Sprinkle [[2 tbsp]] coarse salt over the ribs and flank steak.
Place the short ribs bone side down on the grate away from the hottest coals. Cover and cook for [[90 minutes]], turning every 30 minutes, until tender and well browned.
Add the sausages after the ribs have cooked 40 minutes. Turn them often until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C).
Grill the flank steak over the hot coals for 4 to 5 minutes per side for medium. Rest it for 10 minutes, then slice against the grain.
Check that the ribs are tender enough to pull from the bone. Cut everything into serving pieces.
Serve with [[1 cup]] chimichurri and bread.
Wash the parsley and dry it very well, then chop it finely.
Mince the garlic cloves as small as you can.
Stir the parsley, garlic, [[2 tsp]] oregano, [[1 tsp]] red pepper flakes and [[0.5 tsp]] salt together in a bowl.
Add [[3 tbsp]] red wine vinegar and [[2 tbsp]] warm water and stir.
Pour in [[0.5 cup]] olive oil and mix well.
Let the sauce sit at least [[10 minutes]] so the flavors blend.
Taste and add more salt or vinegar if needed. Serve over grilled meat.
Pound the beef cutlets until they are about 1/4 inch thick, then season with [[1 tsp]] salt and [[0.5 tsp]] pepper.
Beat the eggs in a shallow dish with the minced garlic and [[2 tbsp]] parsley.
Put [[1.5 cups]] breadcrumbs on a plate.
Dip each cutlet in the egg mixture, then press it firmly into the breadcrumbs on both sides.
Rest the breaded cutlets on a rack for [[10 minutes]] so the coating sticks.
Heat [[1 cup]] oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat until a breadcrumb sizzles right away.
Fry the cutlets 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden, working in batches. Drain on paper towels.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.
Rub [[0.5 cup]] cold butter into [[3 cups]] flour and [[1 tsp]] salt with your fingers until crumbly. Stir in [[0.5 cup]] warm water to form a dough.
Knead the dough briefly, wrap it and chill for [[30 minutes]].
Heat [[1 tbsp]] oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the ground beef, [[1 tsp]] cumin, [[1 tsp]] paprika and [[0.5 tsp]] salt. Cook until browned and cooked through to 160°F (71°C), about 8 minutes. Let it cool.
Mix the olives and chopped eggs into the cooled beef filling.
Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C). Roll the dough 1/8 inch thick and cut out 5 inch circles.
Put a spoonful of filling in the center of each circle, fold over and press the edges, then crimp with a fork.
Place the empanadas on a lined baking sheet and brush with beaten egg.
Bake for [[25 minutes]] until golden brown. Cool 5 minutes before eating.

ing: about 9 inch, store-bought or homemade, torn in chunks
st: Heat the oven to 225°F (110°C) and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Beat the egg whites and [[0.25 tsp]] cream of tartar to soft peaks, then add [[1 cup]] sugar a spoonful at a time until stiff and glossy.
Spoon the meringue into rough mounds on the sheet and bake for [[75 minutes]] until dry and crisp. Turn off the oven and let them cool inside.
Whip [[1.5 cups]] cream with [[1 tsp]] vanilla to soft peaks.
Break the cooled meringues into chunks.
Spread a layer of sponge cake chunks in a serving dish and drizzle with some of the [[0.5 cup]] dulce de leche.
Add layers of peaches, whipped cream and meringue, repeating until used up.
Finish with cream, a drizzle of dulce de leche and meringue pieces. Serve at once so the meringue stays crisp.
Pour [[2 l]] milk into a large heavy pot, much bigger than the milk, because it foams up.
Stir in [[2 cups]] sugar and [[0.25 tsp]] baking soda.
Bring to a gentle boil over medium heat, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Lower the heat to a steady low simmer and cook uncovered for [[90 minutes]], stirring often with a wooden spoon.
After it turns light tan and thickens, stir constantly to prevent scorching, for about [[30 minutes]] more.
When it is deep caramel and a spoon drawn across the bottom leaves a clear trail, remove from the heat.
Stir in [[1 tsp]] vanilla.
Cool, then pour into a jar. It thickens more as it cools. Keep refrigerated for up to 2 weeks.
Mix [[3 cups]] flour, [[2 tbsp]] sugar and [[1 tsp]] salt in a large bowl.
Add [[3 tbsp]] melted butter and [[0.75 cup]] warm milk and stir into a soft dough.
Knead on a floured counter for 5 minutes until smooth.
Cover the dough and let it rest for [[30 minutes]].
Roll the dough about 1/4 inch thick and cut into 4 inch rounds. Poke a small slit in each center.
Heat [[3 cups]] oil in a deep pan to 350°F (175°C).
Fry the rounds for 2 minutes per side until puffed and golden. Drain on paper towels.
Dust with sugar while warm and serve.
Heat [[2 cups]] water to about 175°F (80°C), just before boiling.
Fill a mate gourd or large mug about two thirds full with [[0.5 cup]] yerba mate.
Cover the opening with your hand, turn the gourd upside down and shake gently so the fine dust moves to the top.
Tilt the gourd to a slant, so the leaves pile on one side and leave a hollow on the other.
Pour a little warm water into the hollow and let the leaves soak it up.
Place a metal straw with a filter into the hollow, then pour hot water into the same spot.
Sip all the liquid, then refill with hot water. Add [[1 tsp]] sugar if you want it sweeter.
Mix the tomatoes, bell pepper and onion with [[2 tbsp]] vinegar, [[2 tbsp]] olive oil, oregano, parsley and a pinch of salt for the salsa criolla. Let it sit 20 minutes.
Pat the skirt steak dry and rub with [[2 tsp]] coarse salt. Rest at room temperature for 20 minutes while you prepare the fire.
Light hardwood charcoal and burn it down until glowing and covered in gray ash. Spread the coals and set the grate 4 inches above them.
Grill the steak over high heat for 3 minutes per side without moving it until well charred outside and 130°F to 135°F inside for medium rare.
Rest the steak 5 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain.
Warm the garlic in [[2 tbsp]] olive oil for 1 minute, pour it over the sliced meat and serve with the salsa criolla.
nt: Grilled over hot wood or charcoal embers, quick high heat
Best swap: sear in a smoking cast iron pan 2 to 3 minutes per side. Flank steak or hanger steak replaces skirt.
